extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, patent attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating, entering, or denying preliminary, supplemental, and other amendments and replies during patent prosecution (including time limits, form requirements, fee issues, and actions after final). Directed at examiners but also informs applicants on requirements for responsive replies and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment cancelling all claims (not entered)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files a preliminary amendment seeking cancellation of all claims without presenting any new claims, the Office will not enter such an amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Exxon Corp. v. Phillips Petroleum Co., 37 CFR 1.115(b)(1), and MPEP § 601.01(e). Application will not be denied a filing date because such an amendment was submitted on filing. For fee calculation purposes, the Office will treat the application as containing only a single claim. Most such amendments will not meet 37 CFR 1.121(c) (complete claim listing) and the Office will send a notice of non-compliant amendment (37 CFR 1.121) and require an amendment in compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment entry disapproved if unduly interferes with Office action preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry of a preliminary amendment may be disapproved if it unduly interferes with preparation of the first Office action under 37 CFR 1.115(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to file all preliminary amendments as soon as possible. Entry will not be disapproved if filed no later than: (A) 3 months from the filing date under 37 CFR 1.53(b); (B) 3 months from national stage entry under 1.491 for international apps; (C) filing date of a CPA under 1.53(d) in a design app; or (D) last day of any suspension period requested under 1.103. These periods are not extendable (see 1.115(b)(4)). If filed after these periods, entry may be denied subject to SPE approval if other conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-condition test for denying entry of preliminary amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry of a preliminary amendment may be denied only if (1) the examiner has devoted a significant amount of time preparing an Office action before receipt, and (2) entry would require significant additional time to prepare the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receipt date is the 37 CFR 1.6 receipt date. Examples satisfying condition (1): examiner has conducted prior art search or drafted an Office action. Examples satisfying condition (2): amendment amends claims, adds numerous new claims, changes specification to change scope of claims, introduces new matter, includes arguments, includes affidavits/declarations under 1.131/1.132, or includes evidence traversing rejections from parent application and would require another prior art search or extensive revision of Office action. This list is not exhaustive. SPE approval required before denying entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: When disapproval of entry is inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry should not be denied if examiner has not devoted significant preparation time before receipt or if entry would not require significant additional time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if examiner has devoted significant time, disapproval is inappropriate if amendment merely cancels pending claims; amends claims to overcome 35 U.S.C. 112 second paragraph; amends claims to place application in condition for allowance; or only includes changes previously suggested by the examiner that would not require significant additional time. In such cases, the amendment should be entered and considered. See MPEP § 714.19 for other reasons an amendment may be denied entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph for denial due to undue interference (7.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.46 to notify applicant when entry of a preliminary amendment is denied because it unduly interferes with preparation of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph requires bracketed insertions: [1] date Office received amendment (37 CFR 1.6 date), [2] state of preparation of Office action at receipt (e.g., 'claim analysis and prior art search of all pending claims' or 'drafting of Office action awaiting SPE approval'), [3] explanation of how entry would require significant additional time (e.g., 'conduct prior art search in another classification area' or 'revise the Office action extensively to address new issues and new claims'). Advises applicant to file a responsive reply under 1.111/1.113 to avoid abandonment and to resubmit amendment with a reply if not final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply must be fully responsive and specific (37 CFR 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to reconsideration or further examination, reply must be reduced to writing and must distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the examiner's action and reply to every ground of objection and rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply must present arguments pointing out specific distinctions believed to render claims (including newly presented claims) patentable over applied references. A general allegation that claims define a patentable invention without specifics does not comply. Applicant may request that objections not necessary to consideration of claims be held in abeyance. Replies must appear bona fide attempts to advance the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reply must show patentable novelty and avoid references
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending in reply to a rejection, the applicant must clearly point out the patentable novelty the claims present and show how the amendments avoid applied references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to new claims as well; requirements of 37 CFR 1.111(b) must be complied with when presenting arguments in support of new claims and amendments. If lacking, an amendment may be held not fully responsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete replies must comply with formal requirements or traverse them
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reply must either comply with formal requirements or specifically traverse each formal requirement not complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawing and specification corrections, new oaths, etc., are generally formal matters, but the line between formal matters and merits is not sharp; examiners may insist upon formal corrections prior to indicating allowable subject matter if necessary to determine merits. Filing of drawing corrections in reply to objections cannot normally be held in abeyance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of claim amendments permitted (37 CFR 1.121(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be amended by canceling particular claims, presenting new claims, or rewriting particular claims as indicated in 37 CFR 1.121(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements of 1.111(b) must be followed in presenting arguments supporting new claims and amendments. An amendment after a second or subsequent non-final action that increases the number of claims previously acted upon is not to be held not fully responsive for that reason alone (see 37 CFR 1.112).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment not complying with 1.121(b),(c),(d),(h) may be not fully responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment that does not comply with 37 CFR 1.121 subsections may be held not fully responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance can trigger treatment under MPEP § 714 and possible notices of non-compliant amendment (PTOL-324).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment options for amendments not fully responsive (37 CFR 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is not fully responsive, examiner may: (A) accept it as adequate reply (avoiding abandonment), (B) notify applicant to complete the reply within remaining period to avoid abandonment, or (C) set a new time period under 1.135(c) to complete the reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice depends on whether the amendment is bona fide, whether sufficient time remains for applicant's reply, and the nature of the deficiency. If the amendment substantially responds but has a minor deficiency, examiner may act on it and reiterate unaddressed rejections in the new action. For serious deficiencies (e.g., unsigned), if sufficient time remains, notify applicant to supply omission within period; if insufficient time, set a new 1-month period under 1.135(c). Examiner should not further examine merits until omission is timely supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1.135(c) applies only to inadvertent omissions (bona fide replies)
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of giving applicant a new time period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) applies only when a missing matter or lack of compliance is considered inadvertently omitted in a bona fide attempt to advance the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate omissions (e.g., failing to elect species because applicant believes the requirement improper) are not bona fide under 1.135(c) and examiner cannot postpone decision as to abandonment. Once inadvertence is brought to applicant's attention, inadvertence no longer exists and a second 1-month notice would not be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1.135(c) practice not available after final Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.135(c) practice of granting a new time to supply an omission does not apply after a final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after final are approved for entry only if they place the application in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal; otherwise denied entry. Where submission after final does not place application in condition for allowance, the period for reply under 1.113 continues to run until a proper reply is filed. Examiner may request authorization for examiner's amendment to correct omission when reply substantially places application in condition for allowance; in that case date of reply is date of authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner discretion regarding replies after final
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner may enter the reply, withdraw finality of the last Office action, and issue a new Office action (non-final or final) or take action closing prosecution, at the examiner's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These actions (e.g., Ex parte Quayle practice) are solely within the discretion of the examiner. Applicant remains responsible to provide a complete reply under 37 CFR 1.113 when under a final Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee informality and excess claims fees (notification and payment)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment to a non-final Office action presents additional claims and there is an informality as to the fee, technical support staff notifies applicant; excess claims fees must be paid before examiner considers new claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant required to pay excess claims fees for each claim beyond limits (in excess of 3 independent claims or in excess of 20 total claims). Fees for proper multiple dependent claims calculated per 37 CFR 1.75(c); separate fee required for each application containing a multiple dependent claim. Example provided illustrating calculation when claims cancelled and added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs 7.95 / 7.95.01 for bona fide but non-responsive amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.95 (and optionally 7.95.01) where a bona fide reply to a non-final Office action is not fully responsive; applicant given a one-month (or 30 days, whichever longer) time period to supply omission to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Examiner note: practice not applicable where omission deliberate or under final Office action. 7.95.01 (lack of arguments) should be preceded by 7.95 and is primarily for pro se applications; directs applicant to submit arguments under 'Remarks' discussing references and claim distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies not entered as a matter of right (37 CFR 1.111(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply supplemental to a reply in compliance with 1.111(b) will not be entered as a matter of right except in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental reply may be entered if clearly limited to: (A) cancellation of claim(s); (B) adoption of examiner suggestion(s); (C) placement in condition for allowance; (D) reply to an Office requirement made after first reply; (E) correction of informalities (typographical errors); or (F) simplification of issues for appeal. A supplemental reply filed during a period when action is suspended under 1.103(a) or (c) will be entered. Applicants encouraged to include a complete, fully responsive reply to prevent need for supplemental replies. Supplemental replies reduce accumulated patent term adjustment under 1.704(c)(8). If not approved for entry, examiner should notify applicant (form paragraph 7.147 available).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of supplemental replies received after mail date
rubrics_metrics.description: If a supplemental reply is received after the mail date of an Office action and is not responsive to that Office action, the Office will not mail a new Office action responsive to that supplemental reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a courtesy, applicant may be notified that the supplemental reply is nonresponsive and that a timely responsive reply to the mailed Office action must be filed to avoid abandonment. See MPEP § 714.05 when Office action crosses in the mail with a supplemental reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims presented without attempt to point out patentable novelty (not allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amended claims presented without attempt to point out the patentable novelty should not be allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an amendment may be held not fully responsive and a time period set to furnish a proper reply if statutory period expired or nearly expired; however, if claims as amended are clearly open to rejection on record, a final rejection should generally be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate inspection of amendments filed near end of period
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions by applicant filed near the end of the period for reply should be inspected immediately on filing to determine whether they are completely responsive and to prevent abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should check: (A) amendment properly signed (see MPEP § 714.01(a)); (B) filed within statutory or shortened period or time limit (MPEP § 710 - § 710.05); (C) amendment fully responsive and complies with 37 CFR 1.121 (MPEP § 714); (D) whether changes warrant transfer (MPEP § 903.08(d)); (E) whether application is special (MPEP § 708.01); (F) if claims suggested for interference have been copied (Chapter 2300); (G) traversal of restriction requirement (MPEP § 818.03(a)); (H) use of nonpermanent ink (MPEP § 714.07); (I) whether applicant cited references (MPEP § 707.05(b) & § 1302.12); (J) if a terminal disclaimer filed (MPEP §§ 804.02, 804.03, 1490); (K) if any security-related matter added (MPEP § 115). If amendment crosses with action, prepare supplemental action specifying disregarded portions and that reply period runs from mailing of supplemental action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not in permanent ink (1.52(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.52(a) requires permanent dark ink (or equivalent) on papers that become part of the record; 'easily erasable' paper violates requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If noncompliance discovered when amendment reaches Technology Center, applicant promptly notified that amendment not entered and required to file permanent copy within one month or authorize USPTO to make a copy at applicant's expense. Physical entry will be made from permanent copy. If discovered later when application reached for action, similar steps taken but action not held up; requirement for permanent copy included in Office action. Good direct or indirect copies (photocopy, facsimile) on satisfactory paper acceptable. See MPEP § 608.01 for acceptable copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims added in excess of previously paid-for claims (excess claim fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must pay excess claims fees for each claim that is in excess of previously paid-for claims (limits: >3 independent claims or >20 total claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees for a proper multiple dependent claim are calculated based on the number of claims to which it refers (37 CFR 1.75(c)); a separate fee is required for each application containing a proper multiple dependent claim. When applicant adds a new excess claim beyond the number previously paid for (after accounting for canceled claims), excess claims fees must be paid before examiner considers the new claim. Example provided illustrating calculation when claims canceled and added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after final action (37 CFR 1.116) — permissible types
rubrics_metrics.description: After a final rejection or other final action but before appeal, amendments may be admitted in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted: (1) amendments canceling claims or complying with form requirements set forth in previous Office action; (2) amendments presenting rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal; (3) amendments touching the merits may be admitted upon showing good and sufficient reasons why necessary and not earlier presented. Admission or refusal to admit amendments after final does not relieve application from appeal condition or save from abandonment. Special rules apply for reexamination and inter partes reexamination regarding cancellation affecting scope of other pending claims (see details in 1.116(d)).
